findings.title: Reality that holds against falsehood
findings.claim: The focus names Allah as al-Haqq and the invoked alternatives as al-Batil: reality with a basis stands against what lacks one. The pericope's later promise is also called haqq, extending that contrast to what can be relied on.
findings.mechanism: Al-Haqq and al-Batil are explicit opposing carriers in the focus. The call verb makes the contrast audible as speech, letting the restricted well-constructed-speech facet color the truth claim; 31:33 then repeats haqq for Allah's promise. Together these contacts make the contrast about what holds under scrutiny, not only two labels.
findings.reader_payoff: Truth becomes perceptible as a coherent, durable reality that can be trusted, while the calls to alternatives lack that footing.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading that Allah is true and calls to others are false stays intact. The weave and well-formed-speech image is an analogical, form-limited resonance: no textile is named, and the verse does not assert that every invocation has no effect. The 31:33 link is pericope context, not a new morphology claim.

epistemic.reason: The focus opposition, branch records, and channel supports are supplied and trusted. The structural and speech facets of the collocational branch are contextual images, and the 31:33 connection has exact Arabic but no target morphology.

findings.title: Other calls beneath the High
findings.claim: The phrase min dunihi can retain its ordinary sense of calling on others while also placing those targets beneath the High. In the pericope, Allah is acknowledged as creator and owner, so al-Haqq, al-Ali, and al-Kabir give the call's destination a measure of rightful authority and rank.
findings.mechanism: Yadu'una carries a directed call; min dunihi marks the addressees as other-than and, alongside al-Ali, below. The focus's high and great titles independently answer that relation. The creator admission in 31:25, universal ownership in 31:26, and exclusive knowledge at 31:34 make the contact about who has authority, not merely physical height.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the target of the call matters: the invoked alternatives are outside and below the one named as High and Great, whose ownership and knowledge extend beyond them.
findings.containment: Besides-Him remains the ordinary reading, with below and rank as concurrent macro resonances. No physical distance, failed response to every invocation, or legal ruling is asserted. The ownership and knowledge links are contextual readings from exact Arabic whose target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The candidate's trusted supports nominate the distinct call, other, lower, high, and greatness branches; exact pericope Arabic supplies creator, ownership, and knowledge triggers. The vertical and entitlement relations remain contextual rather than morphological claims.

findings.title: Sovereignty across scale and motion
findings.claim: The titles al-Ali and al-Kabir remain high and great, while 31:27-29 lets them name authority that is not measured by the scale of words, the number of created beings, or the height and duration of celestial cycles. The ending's hidden horizons in 31:34 extends that authority beyond what people can know.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace contacts al-Haqq with the ordered structure of 31:27-29, al-Ali with subjection and motion in 31:29, and al-Kabir with words that do not exhaust, many made and raised as one, and cycles bounded by a term. The scale comparison changes greatness from one largest item in a fixed hierarchy to majesty over changing processes. The supplied 31:34 connection adds the Hour, tomorrow, and death-place as knowledge beyond human reach.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing titles become the source of an order that changes and moves under limits, while remaining beyond measurement by number, duration, or celestial height.
findings.containment: The ordinary high and great titles remain recoverable; the trace does not deny physical or quantitative senses. The alternative recorded by the HFT source also remains: the signs may evidence the titles while ordinary magnitude and height stay primary. Context roots, word indices, and roles from the legacy_unbound HFT are attributed; unresolved branch glosses and facets are not supplied and are left null.

findings.title: The creator they already name
findings.claim: The pericope lets al-Haqq echo the audience's own answer that Allah created the heavens and earth; the calls directed elsewhere then read as a contradiction in practice, not simply a failure to know who created.
findings.mechanism: The focus word al-Haqq carries a truth-affirming facet. In 31:25 the supplied Arabic says that, when asked who created the heavens and earth, they will surely say Allah; the connection note links that admission with turning elsewhere. This separate act of affirmation contacts al-Haqq and changes the title from an abstract predicate to a truth they already voice.
findings.reader_payoff: The rebuke becomes a mismatch between what the audience can say about the Creator and where it directs its appeal.
findings.containment: The focus does not quote 31:25 or say that every person named there uses the same theological wording. This is a pericope-level reading from supplied Arabic and a connection note, not a claim that al-Haqq lexically means proof or affirmation.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic for 31:25 is supplied and the trusted channel evidence connects creator recognition with calls elsewhere. The audience-level identity and branch activation are contextual inferences; target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyin doğru olduğunu belirleyip onu doğru diye onaylama işlemi çekirdeği oluşturur.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: In 31:25 the audience is asked who created the heavens and earth and is said to answer Allah; the focus separately names calls to others.
branch_activations.activation: The admission of Allah as creator contacts al-Haqq while the call to alternatives supplies the contrasting act.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Al-Haqq becomes the truth they already voice, which makes the other-directed call a practical contradiction.
branch_activations.boundary: 31:25 states creator recognition, not the exact phrase al-Haqq; this remains a contextual affirmation reading, not a new lexical gloss.
